doc.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022

title: Wanting to be an arranger and respect for arrangers
summary: Tiberi says he was content but wishes he had been schooled as an arranger.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Did you aspire to — while you were doing the shows, you’re making a good living but musicians often times are, they seem like they’re constantly looking for the next thing. Like what I’m doing now is pretty good but I would really like to do — and did you have that feeling that you wanted to do something else?

No not at all, no. I was just particularly concerned of being able to do things that I planned out myself and to be, actually — to use a concept that I’m doing right now and I’m able to teach to students, and to be good in that area.

You know I’d like to be a great arranger but I’m not schooled for that actually. What I can do is, the way I learned was to you know get all the charts and just see what it was and then that was my — but it would have been good if I’d had another life I think I would you know be an arranger. I mean a musician/arranger such as all the cats that I mentioned.
I know what you mean, arranging is a wonderful thing and you can leave a legacy of charts for other people to play.

That’s always good. I always respected even the arrangers and the back-up singers and all that, what they do. I mean that’s a hell of a trait I’ll tell you that. I mean you’ve got to be really talented to be able to really do that.
